comments.text: The processor port's direction register, left as the KERNAL set it.
The processor port: $1900 clears bit 0, leaving $36, so BASIC is out of the map and the KERNAL and I/O stay; the cracker's saver sets $37.
Pointer to the unused tune player's note data ($1050 sets it to $8200), and $04 its offset; the game itself clears $02-$52 at start ($1170).
High byte of the unused tune player's note pointer.
Offset into the unused tune's note data; the pointer at $02 moves on a page when it wraps.
Note lengths left for the three voices of the unused tune player ($05-$07).
Note length left for the unused tune's second voice.
Note length left for the unused tune's third voice.
Waveform and gate of voice 1 for the unused tune player; $09 and $0A hold voices 2 and 3.
Set to 1 when flak rises and to $80 when it bursts ($2680, $2700), but nothing reads it: a sound trigger with no player. The unused tune player keeps voice 2's waveform here.
The shot sound's step counter: $1E40 sets it to 1, $2600 counts it to $38. The unused tune player keeps voice 3's waveform here.
Voice being worked on by the unused tune player's tick ($10A0).
Frequency high byte of the note the unused tune player is setting up; $0D the low byte.
Frequency low byte of the note the unused tune player is setting up.
First byte of the note pair the unused tune player has just read; $0F the second.
Second byte of the note pair: bits 0-2 the octave, bits 3-7 the length.
Pointer to the sound chip voice ($D400 + 7n) the unused tune player is writing; $11 its high byte.
High byte of the voice pointer, $D4.
Set when the unused tune reaches its end marker; its interrupt then starts the tune again.
The score, five decimal digits from the highest ($13-$17), each 0-9 and shown directly as the digit characters 0-9.
The score's last digit, to which $2540 adds the points before carrying.
Screen pointer: the hill row being scrolled ($1550) or the highscore row ($1210, $12D0); $19 its high byte.
High byte of the screen pointer at $18.
Colour RAM pointer for the highscore row ($1256); $1B its high byte.
High byte of the colour pointer at $1A.
Cursor position in the name entry's alphabet, 0-27 ($12D0).
Letters entered so far in the name entry, up to twelve.
Counts passes of the main loop ($1466); the movement rates mask it to decide what moves on each pass.
The joystick reading of this pass ($1920): bit 4 fire, bits 0-3 up, down, left, right, clear while pressed.
The raster interrupt's band, 0 sky, 1 ground, 2 status panel ($13AB).
Counts calls of the hill scroll, so the slow speeds act every other call ($1500, $2220).
Scroll speed and direction set by the stick: -2 to +2, positive when the stick is right ($193C).
Fine horizontal scroll of the hill rows, 0-7 ($1500, $14C0).
Colour RAM pointer of the hill row being scrolled ($1550); $25 its high byte.
High byte of the colour pointer at $24.
Second record pointer: a template ($1650, $19F0, $1E20, $2660, $28A0), the hill panorama ($1550), the shot record in a hit, or the level's target pictures from $8B80 ($2B5A); $27 its high byte.
High byte of the pointer at $26.
Column of the 40-column hill panorama at the screen's edge, 0-39 ($15C0, $1600).
Scratch byte: a step, a sort key, a column.
Scratch byte: a sprite's bit mask, a record number, whether a record moved.
Scratch byte: a sprite number in a band, a bar width.
Scratch byte for an explosion picture.
Hill rows left to scroll ($1550 sets 3).
Pointer to the record being worked on, set by $1630, $19D0, $1E00, $2130, $2640; $2F its high byte.
High byte of the record pointer at $2E.
Number of the record being worked on, counted down by each family's loop.
Template number for $1650 and $28A0.
Ground objects that moved this pass ($1720); when 0 the sort is skipped.
The noise voice's output this pass ($1920), the game's main random number.
CIA1 timer A high byte this pass, a second random number.
CIA1 timer A low byte this pass.
The raster line this pass, a fourth random number.
Climb rate, -1, 0 or +1: +1 moves the plane up the screen, so the stick pulled down climbs ($193C, $1990).
Template number for $19F0, $1E20 and $2660.
Enemy aircraft that moved this pass ($1AD9).
The movement bits of the record being moved (byte 10 masked with $1E).
Shots that moved this pass ($1F00).
The movement bits of the shot being moved.
Sprite-sprite collisions in the sky band, latched by the interrupt and cleared by the hit test.
Sprite-sprite collisions in the ground band, latched by the interrupt and cleared by the hit test.
The plane's crash: 0 flying, then counts up from 1 to $A0 while it explodes ($2400).
Lives: 4 at the start, 9 at most; the game ends when it goes below 0.
The kind of ground defence being fought, 0-3, and the picture set of the ground objects; $80 during the strafing runs.
Hits still needed before the next kind of defence: 5, 10, 20 or 20 by level at the start of a kind; any hit counts, ground or air.
Planes left for the strafing runs, counted down from the lives to 0.
The level, 0-3; after 3 it goes back to 0.
Hits on the target in the strafing runs, shown as three digits; it decides the result.
The music driver's pointers: $FB/$FC the track, $FD/$FE the pattern ($A006). The cracker's save uses $FB/$FC for the start address.
High byte of the music's track pointer.
Pointer to the music pattern being read, $FE its high byte.
High byte of the music's pattern pointer.

Cracker's highscore file image, the part H.PATROL HI /REM loads at $0C00: five rows of five score digits ($0C00, $0C05, $0C0A, $0C0F, $0C14), then five names of twelve letters from $0C19. $0C55 refills it from the table on screen before saving.
The second highscore row's five digits in the cracker's file image.
The third highscore row's five digits in the cracker's file image.
The fourth highscore row's five digits in the cracker's file image.
The fifth highscore row's five digits in the cracker's file image.
The five highscore names of the cracker's file image, twelve screen codes each ($0C19, $0C25, $0C31, $0C3D, $0C49).
The second highscore name, twelve screen codes, in the cracker's file image.
The third highscore name in the cracker's file image.
The fourth highscore name in the cracker's file image.
The fifth highscore name in the cracker's file image.

Cracker's highscore saver, run after a name is entered ($136B): puts the system interrupt back, copies the five scores and names from the title screen at $4122 + n*$50 into $0C00-$0C54, and saves $0C00-$0C54 to drive 8 as "@S:H.PATROL HI /REM" (name at $0CF0) through the KERNAL, then restarts at $1450.
The save command and file name for $0C55, 19 characters: "@S:H.PATROL HI /REM" (the @S: replaces the old file).

The cracker's level-skip trainer: the menu's yes changes the call at $1934 from $0D14 to here. Every 8th pass, unless the plane is crashing, a port B reading of $DF (the C= key while $DC00 selects row 7, where the KERNAL leaves it) sets the target hits $45 to 64 and jumps into the strafing runs' end ($2AA7), as if the target had been destroyed; otherwise it reads the stick as $0D14 does.
Returns CIA1 port B ($DC01), the joystick in port 1, in A: bit 4 fire, bits 0-3 up, down, left, right, each clear while pressed.
Set to $80 when the shot sound ends ($2600); nothing reads it.

Tail of the hit test ($23D5 jumps here): when the plane's sprite touched one of sprites 4-7 in the sky band ($3D bit 0 and bits 4-7), finds that enemy aircraft and, if it is near (byte 6 at least 9) and not already exploding, marks it hit ($40) and starts the plane's crash ($3F = 1). Then clears both collision latches and redraws the distance bar ($29E0).

Returns in $2B the hits-needed count of the current level ($42 at the start of a kind) shifted left by one for each level below 3: the width, in bar pixels, a whole kind of defence takes in the distance bar ($29E0).
Sets $42, the hits needed to clear the current kind of defence, to 5 shifted left once per level: 5, 10, 20, 20 for levels 0-3 ($44; level 3 is treated as 2).
Unreferenced code left between routines: sets the level $44 to 3 and redraws the target counter ($2DE1). Nothing calls it.
Colours the whole title screen ($4000-$43FF) from each character's code through the table at $8100, then sets the fixed colours of its rows ($11D0).

Start of a small three-voice tune player that nothing in the game calls (no reference to $1000 anywhere in memory, and it never ran in play): points the IRQ vector at $102E, sets CIA1 timer A to $3000 cycles, starts the tune ($1050) and returns.
Interrupt handler of the unused player: restarts the tune when $12 is set (end of data), plays one tick ($10A0), acknowledges the CIA and returns from the interrupt.

Starts the unused player's tune: copies the 25 sound-chip register values at $8010 to $D400, points $02/$03 at the note data $8200, keeps each voice's waveform (with the gate bit) in $08-$0A, and sets the first note's frequency from $8200/$8201.

One tick of the unused player: for each of the three voices, counts down its note length ($05-$07); when one ends it releases the gate, reads the next two bytes of note data at ($02) ($FF ends the tune and sets $12), looks up the frequency in $1145 by the low four bits of the first and doubles it, an octave up, for each step in bits 0-2 of the second, and takes the length from $115F by the second byte's lowest set bit above bit 2.
Frequency table of the unused player, two bytes a note, high byte first: a rest (0), then twelve notes of its lowest octave ($010C ... $00FD), which $10A0 doubles for higher octaves.
Note lengths of the unused player, by the second note byte's high bits: $80, $40, $20, $10, $08 ticks (the byte before, $FD, is the last frequency's low byte).

Selects video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through CIA2 port A, clears zero page $02-$52, then (entry $118B, also used at game over) loads the video chip from the 47-byte register image at $8030, skipping $FF entries, and writes the score to the title screen ($2EE0).
Entry used at game over ($14A9): loads the video chip from $8030 and writes the score to the title screen.

The title and highscore screen, shown before every game: screen $4000 ($D018 = $02), colours it ($0F90), puts the last score in the table if it is high enough ($1210) and runs the name entry ($12D0) when it is; then waits for fire to be pressed and released.

Sets fixed colours on the title screen's colour RAM: blue rows in the middle, a white row and a grey line at the bottom, black over the alphabet row, and the top row from its characters through $8100.

Compares the score digits $13-$17 with the five score rows of the table on the title screen ($4122 + n*$50); at the first row it beats, moves the rows below down ($1256) and returns the row number in Y (0 when the score made no row, or is zero).

Moves the highscore rows below row Y down one place (23 characters each, from the bottom up), writes the score digits and twelve spaces for the name into row Y, and colours that row's line on screen white.

Highscore name entry under the alphabet row: left and right move a white cursor over 28 positions (A-Z and two more), with a delay loop between moves; fire writes the letter into the row, up to twelve; the last position ends the entry. Then it saves the table through the cracker's code at $0C55.

Points the IRQ vector $0314 at $13AB, turns off the CIA interrupts, enables the video chip's raster and sprite-sprite collision interrupts, sets the first raster line to $D2, waits for line $FB and clears the collision latches. The music interrupt is replaced by this one.

Raster interrupt of play, three bands a frame counted in $20. Band 0 loads the sky band's register image from $8060 (all of $D000-$D02E) and its sprite pointers from $8520; band 1 loads the ground band's image from $8090 (from $D008) and pointers from $8528; band 2 sets the status panel (background $0B, raster $FB). Sprite-sprite collisions are latched into $3D in the sky band and $3E in the ground band, each only while the latch is clear.
Entry from the cracker's menu and from the highscore saver: starts the noise voice ($1900), sets up the video chip ($1170), and falls into the game loop.

One whole game per pass: restarts the music ($14F0), shows the title and highscore screen and waits for fire ($11A0), sets up a new game ($14D0) and colours the play screen ($2150), runs the main loop at $1466 until the lives $40 go negative, then reloads the video registers ($118B) and starts again.

One pass of play; the loop has no wait of its own. Steers ($193C), spawns and moves the ground objects ($1670), counts the pass in $1E, sets the scroll register ($14C0), sorts the ground objects into sprites ($17A0), reads the inputs ($1920), moves the plane ($1990), moves the enemy aircraft ($1A10, $1BFD), the shots ($1E80, $1F8D), the ground stripes ($2900), resolves hits ($2F00), runs the crash ($2400), the engine sound ($25A0) and the flak ($2700). It ends when $40 is negative.
Writes the fine horizontal scroll ($23, 0-7) with the 38-column bit clear and multicolour on ($10) into both register images' $D016 ($8076, $80A6).
Copies the third row of the hill panorama ($8F00) to screen row 7 ($4518) and sets up a new game ($24F0).
Clears the sound chip's filter routing and starts the title music ($A000).

Called every 8th pass by $1670. At scroll speed $22 of $02 or $FE it scrolls every time, at $01 or $FF every other time ($21 counts the calls). Right ($22 positive) steps the fine scroll $23 down, and after 8 steps waits for raster line $60 and moves the hill rows one character left ($15C0); left steps it up and moves them right ($1600).
Sets the pointers for the hill scroll: screen $44C8 and colour RAM $D8C8 (row 5), three rows ($2D), and the panorama source $8D00.
Unreferenced code: an earlier version of $2F80 that took the panorama column 39 places on for the right edge. Nothing calls it.
Moves the screen and colour pointers $18 and $24 down one row (40 characters).
Moves the three hill rows one character left on screen and in colour RAM, and fills the right edge from the panorama ($2F80) with the column number $28 increased by one.
Moves the three hill rows one character right on screen and in colour RAM, and fills the left edge from the panorama ($2FB0) with the column number $28 decreased by one.

Sets $2E/$2F to ground object record $30 (16 bytes each) of the table at $80C0: the four ground objects in normal play, the three parts of the target in a strafing run. Byte 0 is the depth (0 free), 1 x, 2 y, 3 x high bit, 4-5 expand flags, 6 next template, 7 sideways rate, 8 approach rate, 9 picture, 15 kind and the hit bit $40.
Sets $26/$27 to template $31 (16 bytes each) of the ground objects' table at $8400.

Starts a ground object in the first free record of $80C0 when the voice 3 random number $33 has its low seven bits zero: on the horizon (y $73), at x $61 plus seven random bits of the raster line, of the current kind $41. Then advances each record whose depth has reached its next template ($8400): takes the template's sizes, rates and picture. Ends by moving ($1720) and freeing ($1780) them.

Scrolls the hills every 8th pass ($1500), then moves each ground object sideways with the scroll ($2220) and, when its approach rate is due, one step nearer: its depth and y both grow by the rate, so it comes down the screen. $32 counts the objects that moved.
Frees each ground object whose depth has reached $58: it has passed under the plane.
Resolves hits ($2F00), then falls into $17A3.

Unless a strafing run is on ($41 negative), sorts the ground objects by y into the list at $8500 and writes them to sprites 4-7 of the ground band: x, y, x high bit, enable, the expand bits and the picture. The picture is the template's picture plus 10 for each kind ($0F bits 0-1); a hit object shows explosion picture $C0 + 2 x (picture - $5D), alternating every 4 passes.
Starts CIA1 timer A, sets voice 3 of the sound chip to noise at frequency $80xx for random numbers, and clears bit 0 of the processor port $01, which takes the BASIC ROM out of the memory map.
Takes random numbers for the pass: the voice 3 output ($D41B) into $33, CIA1 timer A into $35/$34, the raster line into $36. Then reads the stick ($0D14) into $1F.

Unless the plane is crashing, every 8th pass: right raises the scroll speed $22 to at most +2, left lowers it to at least -2, down raises the climb rate $37 to +1, up lowers it to -1; with fire held it fires ($1E40). A rate stays where the stick left it.

Unless crashing: sets the plane's picture in both bands to $42 plus the scroll speed (banked left, level or right), and every other pass moves its y ($8061, $8091) by the climb rate: up the screen to $51 at the highest, down to $A0 at the lowest. Then sets the shadow ($22B0).
Sets $2E/$2F to enemy aircraft record $30 (16 bytes each, four records) of the table at $8530, laid out like the ground objects; byte 10 holds movement bits.
Sets $26/$27 to template $38 (16 bytes each) of the enemy aircraft's table at $8570.

When the random number $33 is zero, starts an enemy aircraft in a free record: depth $36, y $3A, from the left edge or from x $14F on the right by the sign of the pass counter $1E, heading the other way. Then advances each record whose depth matches its next template ($8570) and takes the template's fields; a hit one steps its template back. Ends with $1AD9 and $1BD0.

For each enemy aircraft: moves it with the scroll ($2220); unless it is exploding, moves it left or right by its movement bits (byte 10 bits 4 and 3) and, when due, down or up (bits 2 and 1, $1B9F and $1B8D); every 32 passes, with the random number, turns it round; every 16 passes its depth falls by one, so it moves away. $39 counts the aircraft that moved.
Moves the aircraft up the screen one line unless its y is already below $38.
Moves the aircraft down the screen one line unless its y is already $50 or more.
Frees each enemy aircraft whose depth has fallen to 0.
Resolves hits ($2F00), then falls into $1C00.

Sorts the enemy aircraft by y into the list at $8508 and writes them to sprites 4-7 of the sky band: x, y, x high bit, enable, expand bits, multicolour off; the picture is the template's picture plus 10 when heading left. A hit aircraft shows explosion picture $A2 + 2 x (picture - $4D), multicolour, alternating every 4 passes.
Sets $2E/$2F to shot record $30 (16 bytes each) of the table at $8670.
Sets $26/$27 to template $38 (16 bytes each) of the shots' table at $86A0.
When shot record 0 is free, starts a shot from the plane: x $A0, y the plane's plus 4, moving up the screen (byte 10 = 2), and starts its sound ($0A = 1). Only record 0 is ever used.
Advances each shot whose depth matches its next template ($86A0) and takes the template's fields, then moves them ($1F00) and frees the far ones ($2100).
For each shot: moves it with the scroll ($2220), deepens it when its rate is due, and moves it down or up the screen by byte 10 ($1F5B, $1F65). $3B counts the shots that moved.
Adds $29 to the record's y.
Takes $29 from the record's y.
Resolves hits ($2F00), then falls into $1F90.

Writes shot record 0 into sprite 1 of both bands (x, y, x high bit, enable, expand bits, picture), then copies sprites 1-3's x high, enable, Y expand and X expand bits from the sky band's image into the ground band's.
Frees each of the two shot records whose depth has reached $40, unless its byte 10 has bit 6 set.
Sets $2E/$2F to ground stripe record $30 (three bytes each, twelve records) of the table at $87A0: byte 0 is its byte in the character set at $4907, byte 1 its template, byte 2 its rate.
Colours the whole play screen ($4400-$47FF) from each character's code through the table at $8100.

Moves the record at $2E/$2F sideways by its own rate (byte 7: bit 7 set gives a step of the low bits, otherwise a step of 1 on passes where the bits mask the counter $1E to zero), right when the scroll speed $22 is negative, left when it is positive, and only every other call at speeds $01 and $FF. $2A is 1 when it moved.
Takes $29 from the record's x, flipping its x high bit on a borrow; across the left edge it skips the 8 hidden pixels between x $FF and $F8.
Adds $29 to the record's x, flipping its high bit on a carry; across the right edge it skips the 8 hidden pixels between x $F8 and $FF.
Sets the shadow's picture (sprite 3 of the ground band) from the plane's height: one of five pictures from $87 by ($A0 - y) / 16, plus the scroll speed for its bank.

Resolves hits in normal play from the latches. Sky band ($3D): the shot (sprite 1) on an aircraft (sprites 4-7) clears the shot, sets the aircraft exploding (depth $20, picture $4D), counts a hit off $42 and scores 50. Ground band ($3E): the shot on a ground object clears the shot, sets the object hit, counts a hit off $42 and scores 100. Each hit plays the explosion ($23F5). Then the crash tests: the plane (sprite 0) touching the flak (sprite 2) in the ground band, or the shadow (sprite 3) touching a ground object while the plane is low (shadow picture below $8A), starts the crash; otherwise $0F00 tests the sky band.
Returns in Y twice the number of the lowest set bit of A counted from bit 4: the list position of the first of sprites 4-7 in a collision mask.
Returns in Y twice the number of the lowest set bit of A counted from bit 1: the list position of the shot sprite in a collision mask.
Retriggers voice 3, the noise voice, as the explosion of a hit.

While $3F is not zero the plane is exploding. The first pass loads the crash sound from $8B00 and gates all three voices. Every other pass the plane shows explosion picture $9E plus the high nibble of $3F, multicolour, in colour 6, and $3F counts up; at $A0 a life is taken ($40), the play is reset ($2480) and the plane's colours put back.

Clears the ground objects, aircraft and shots, the scroll and climb, the crash and the collision latches; enables only the plane and the shadow; puts the plane at y $A0; shows the lives on the status line; waits in a delay loop; restarts the engine sound ($2580).

Clears the score, sets four lives and level 0, copies the first two hill rows ($8D00, $8E00) to screen rows 5 and 6. Then (entry $2516, also each new level) fills the distance bar's characters, clears the target hits $45, resets the play, sets the hits needed, starts with kind 0, shows the score, starts the raster interrupt and shows the target count and the level.
Entry for a new level ($2EC3): fills the distance bar's characters and sets the level going, as below.
Adds A to the last score digit and carries through the five decimal digits at $13-$17, then writes them in white to the status line at $4771.
Silences the sound chip, loads all its registers from the 25-byte image at $8850 and starts voice 1 as a pulse wave with ring modulation.
Sets voice 1's frequency and pulse width low bytes from the plane's height inverted, so the engine rises in pitch as the plane climbs; then runs the shot sound twice ($2600).
Stores A as the plane's picture in the ground band and as the shadow's picture.
Plays the shot on voice 2 while the counter $0A runs: retriggers the voice at 1 and every 16 steps, counts on to $38, where it writes $80 to $0E00 and stops.
Sets $2E/$2F to flak record $30 (16 bytes each) of the table at $8880. Only record 0 is used.
Sets $26/$27 to template $38 (16 bytes each) of the flak's table at $88A0.

When the flak record is free, starts a burst rising from y $50 at a random x from voice 3 ($21-$120), drifting right when it starts on the left half and left otherwise, with a burst time in byte 11 of $10-$4F plus timer bits. Sets $09, which nothing reads.

Spawns flak ($2680). While it rises, advances its template ($88A0) when the depth matches, and when its depth reaches the burst time sets byte 11 to $FD. A burst shows pictures $46-$48 (picture $45 plus the low bits of byte 11) every 32 passes as byte 11 counts $FD, $FE, $FF, and frees the record at 0. Then moves it ($2780) and draws it ($2820).
Moves the flak with the scroll and by its movement bits like an aircraft, and while it rises moves it up or down the screen ($280A, $27F8) and deepens it.
Takes $29 from the flak's y.
Adds $29 to the flak's y unless it is already $C2 or more.
Writes the flak to sprite 2 of both bands: x, y, x high bit, picture and enable, or disables sprite 2 when the record is free.
Sets $26/$27 to template $31 (16 bytes each) of the ground stripes' table at $8A00.

Every 32 passes starts a ground stripe in a free record (at byte 1, template 1, rate $1F). Then, for each stripe whose rate is due, draws it one or more character-set bytes further down the ground characters at $4907 (bit pattern $55, $AA or $FF by record number), freeing it past byte $68; a stripe whose position matches its template's takes the template's rate. The stripes run down the ground like furrows passing under the plane.

Unless a strafing run is on, draws the progress of the current kind into the distance bar's characters at $4970: each kind takes a 40-pixel section from the right ($78 less $28 per kind), filled in proportion to the hits made ($0F40). When the hits needed $42 reach 0 it sets them for the next kind, counts the kind in $41, and at 4 starts the strafing runs ($2A4C).

The strafing runs: sets $41 to $80 and clears the target hits $45; then for each plane, from the lives left ($43) down to 0, sets up a run ($2B00) and plays it with its own main loop until the target's first part has passed or the plane has crashed. After the last run, or when the lives go negative, shows the result ($2E30) and recolours the screen.

Sets up one strafing run: plane level at y $A0, every object cleared, "STRAFING RUN AIRCRAFT NO." with the number $43, the level's target pictures copied from the source $8B80 gives into the sprite shapes at $7800 (eight pages), "PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE" until fire is pressed and released; then places the target's three parts side by side at x $6C plus seven timer bits, 24 apart, on the horizon.
Reads a byte from $8000 plus the level and throws it away: the next instruction loads 1 over it, so every part's colour (byte 14) is white on every level.

Advances the target's templates ($16BC), then writes its three parts into sprites 4-6 of the ground band; each part's picture is $E0 + 3 x (picture - $5D) + its number. A hit part loses its hit bit at once, and black is written to sprite 5's colour ($80BC) whichever part was hit; every 16th pass each part's colour is set back from its byte 14.

Resolves hits during a strafing run like $22D0: the shot on an aircraft scores 50, the shot on a part of the target scores 100, and each hit counts one on the target ($2DD5). The plane touching the flak, or the shadow touching the target while low, starts the crash.
Returns in Y twice the number of the lowest set bit of A counted from bit 4 (as $23DB).
Returns in Y twice the number of the lowest set bit of A counted from bit 1 (as $23E8).
Plays the explosion and counts a hit on the target ($45), then falls into $2DE1.
Writes the target hits $45 as three digits to the status line ($47BC), and the first five characters of the top highscore row as the high score ($47C1).

After the strafing runs: picks a message by the target hits $45 (64 or more, 48, 16, fewer, through the pointers at $8B90), shows it with "PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE" until fire. With 16 hits or more it gives a life (up to 9) and the next level, from 3 back to 0. Then starts the level again ($2516) and shows "DISTANCE TO TARGET".
Copies the score digits to the title screen at $4023 and the level number to $401B, in white.
Calls $22D0 in normal play and $2CD0 during a strafing run ($41 negative).
RESTORE key restart: reached through the cartridge signature at $8000, which sends the KERNAL's NMI routine here. Resets the stack, the I/O chips ($FDA3) and starts the game again at $1450.

Fills the right-edge character of a hill row from the panorama: column $28 (wrapped to 0 after 39), the character into the screen and its colour from $8100 into colour RAM; then moves the source to the next row's page.
Fills the left-edge character of a hill row from the panorama: column $28 (wrapped to 39 below 0), the character and its colour; then moves the source to the next row's page.
The first level's target, a long low building drawn as three sprites side by side, in its sizes from far to near: 32 sprite shapes copied to $7800 for a strafing run ($2B00).
The first level's target, the nearer sizes (second half of the set).
The second level's target, 32 sprite shapes copied to $7800 for a strafing run.
The second level's target, the nearer sizes.

The title screen, 1000 screen codes shown with $D018 = $02: row 0 "BATTLE STATISTICS TARGET 00 SCORE 00000", the HUNTER PATROL logo in rows 2-5, the highscore table in rows 7-15, the name prompt in row 17, "PRESS FIRE TO START", the alphabet in a box in rows 20-22, and the credit line.
The level digit after "TARGET" on the title screen ($2EE0).
The score digits on the title screen, five ($2EE0), and the rest of row 0.
Title screen from row 6, column 16: the second quarter of the screen that $0F90 colours a page at a time.
The first highscore row on the title screen: the rank, five score digits at $4122 and twelve name letters from $412B, one row in every two ($50 apart).
The first highscore name on the title screen.
The second highscore row's score digits.
The second highscore name.

The third highscore name.
Title screen from row 12, column 32, the third page that $0F90 colours.

The fifth highscore name, then row 16, the prompt "WELL DONE - PLEASE ENTER YOUR NAME" in row 17, "PRESS FIRE TO START" in row 18 ($42D0) and the start of row 19.
Title screen from row 19, column 8: the alphabet box and the credit line "(C)MASTERTRONIC 1985 WRITTEN BY STEVE LEE".

Play screen rows 8-19: each row is filled with one ground character, $21 in row 8 down to $2C in row 19, so redrawing a character's eight bytes moves a stripe along the whole row ($2900). Loaded with the game; the code never writes these rows.
Play screen from row 12, column 32, the third page that $2150 colours: more ground rows.

Play screen from row 19, column 8: the last ground row, then the status panel from row 21: SCORE, the distance bar's characters $2E-$41, TARGET, HI, DISTANCE TO TARGET and LIVES, with the digits the code writes.
Status panel between the level digit and the score digits.
Status panel: the rest of row 22 and row 23 up to the message line, "HIT" and "HI" and the start of "DISTANCE TO TARGET".
Status panel between the target hits and the high score.
Status panel: the rest of row 24 up to the lives digit, with "LIVES".
The status panel's last cell after the lives digit.

The character set: the digits 0-9 as codes 0-9 (scores are shown as these codes) and the space at $20. Codes $0A-$1F are on no screen the game draws. The ground characters $21-$2D and the distance bar's $2E-$41 that follow are redrawn by the code.
Last byte of the space character $20, and the base of the ground stripes' writes: a stripe at position n draws byte $4907 + n, from character $21's first byte.
The first byte of ground character $21, set to $FF at the end of each stripe pass ($29C3).
The distance bar's first character, $2E.
Characters $42-$7F, which are on no screen the game draws.

Characters $80-$BF: the full stop and A-Z from $80, then the up arrow, dash and copyright sign; all text is written in these codes. $A0-$B3 are the multicolour hill pieces, and $B5-$BF the digits 5-9 and punctuation of the standard set, unused.
Characters $C0-$FF: the HUNTER PATROL logo of the title screen ($C0-$ED) and the frames round it and round the alphabet ($EE-$F9).
Sprite shapes $40-$4F: the plane banked hard left to hard right ($40-$44), the flak as a dot ($45) and its three bursts ($46-$48), then an enemy aircraft facing right from near to far ($49-$4F).

Sprite shapes $50-$5F: the right-facing aircraft's three smallest sizes ($50-$52), the left-facing one from near to far ($53-$5C), and the first ground kind, a tank, in its three farthest sizes ($5D-$5F).
Sprite shapes $60-$6F: the tank's nearer sizes ($60-$66) and the second ground kind, a lorry, from far to near ($67-$6F).
Sprite shapes $70-$7F: the lorry's nearest size ($70), the third ground kind, a tower, from far to near ($71-$7A), and the fourth, a house, in its farthest sizes ($7B-$7F).
Inside sprite shape $7D, a far house.
Sprite shapes $80-$8F: the house's nearer sizes ($80-$84), then the plane's shadow in its first sizes, five banks to a size ($85-$8F).
Sprite shapes $90-$9F: the shadow's smaller sizes ($90-$9D) and the first two pictures of the plane's crash ($9E-$9F).
Inside sprite shape $9F, the second picture of the crash.

Sprite shapes $A0-$AF: the explosion, a blue burst that grows into a ring and breaks up ($A0-$A7, the end of the crash and a hit aircraft), then the shot, a pair of tracer dots, shrinking as it flies away ($A8-$AF).
Sprite shapes $B0-$BF: the shot's two smallest pictures ($B0-$B1), then shapes $B2-$BF filled almost solid, which nothing shows.
Sprite shapes $C0-$CF: a ground object's explosion in its sizes, each an orange flash and a spray that take turns every four passes.
Sprite shapes $D0-$DF: the explosion's nearest size ($D0-$D1), then solid fillers $D2-$DF, which nothing shows.
Cartridge signature, which makes RESTORE restart the game: the KERNAL's reset and NMI routines look for "CBM80" at $8004 and then jump through $8000 or $8002, both $2F30 here.
The unused tune player's sound chip settings, 25 bytes copied to $D400-$D418 by $1050: sawtooth waves ($20 at $8014, $801B, $8022), each with the envelope $88, $88, and volume 15.
Voice 1's waveform in the unused tune's settings, $20 (sawtooth); $1050 adds the gate bit.

Voice 3's waveform in the unused tune's settings, $20 (sawtooth).

Register image of the sky band, the whole of $D000-$D02E that the interrupt copies at the top of the screen ($13AB): sprite 0 the plane (x $A0, y at $8061), sprite 1 the shot, sprite 2 the flak, sprite 3 the shadow, sprites 4-7 the enemy aircraft; $D018 = $12 puts the screen at $4400.
The plane's height on screen in the sky band, $51 (highest) to $A0 (lowest); $8091 holds the same for the ground band.

Colour of each character, 256 bytes indexed by screen code, used whenever a screen is coloured ($0F90, $2150, $2F80): white for the digits and letters, and the multicolour codes of the ground from $21, of the distance bar's four sections from $2E (5 characters each) and of the hills from $A0.

The unused tune's notes: two bytes a note ($FF ends it at $8346), read by whichever voice finishes first: the low four bits of the first byte pick the note from $1145 (0 a rest), the second byte's bits 0-2 the octave and bits 3-7 the length.
Second byte of the unused tune's first note. The bytes from $8347 to $8368 after the end marker are not read.

The ground objects' templates, 16 bytes each: byte 0 the depth at which an object takes it, 4 and 5 the expand flags, 6 the next template, 7 the sideways rate, 8 the approach rate, 9 the picture. Twelve are used: the object grows from picture $5D to $66 and speeds up as it nears, and the last sends it past at depth $4D.
Base of the shift at $17DC, two bytes before the ground objects' sort list: X runs from 9 down to 2 or more, so the loop reads the list itself and never these two bytes.
Sort list of the ground objects by y: pairs of record number and y, rebuilt each pass ($17A3).
The y of the first pair in the ground sort list.
Base of the shift at $1C32, two bytes before the aircraft's sort list; X is 2 or more, so the loop reads the list itself. These two bytes are the last pair of the ground objects' sort list.
Sort list of the enemy aircraft by y ($1C00).
The y of the first pair in the aircraft's sort list.
Base of the shift at $1FC2, two bytes before the shot's sort list; X is 2 or more, so the loop reads the list itself. These two bytes are the last pair of the aircraft's sort list.
Sort list of the shots by y ($1F90).
The y of the first pair in the shot's sort list.
Sprite pointers of the sky band, copied to $47F8 by the interrupt: $8520 the plane, $8521 the shot, $8522 the flak, $8524-$8527 the aircraft.

Sprite pointers of the ground band: $8528 the plane, $8529 the shot, $852A the flak, $852B the shadow, $852C-$852F the ground objects or the target.
The shot's picture in the ground band.

Pictures of the ground objects, sprites 4-7 in the ground band.
The four enemy aircraft records, 16 bytes each ($19D0).
Second enemy aircraft record.

The enemy aircraft's templates, 16 bytes each, read two below the record's next template because aircraft move away: a new aircraft starts at depth $36 on template 10 ($8610) and steps back through pictures $49 to $52 as its depth falls to 4 ($8570). Facing left adds 10, $53-$5C.
The shot records, 16 bytes each; only the first is used ($1E40).
Second shot record, cleared but never started.
The shots' templates, 16 bytes each: the shot shrinks through pictures $A8-$B1 as it flies away from depth 1 to $58; the record at $8730 is filled with $FF.
Twelve ground stripe records of three bytes ($2130): the byte of the ground characters, the template, the rate. The values loaded here are those of a moment of play.
The engine's sound chip settings, 25 bytes loaded by $2580, which then starts voice 1 as a triangle wave ring-modulated by voice 3; voice 3 is noise at frequency $01C2.
The flak record, 16 bytes ($2640); byte 11 is the burst time.
The flak's templates: the dot picture $45 rises from depth 1 to $58, with the rates changing on the way; the last record holds picture $47.

The ground stripes' templates, 16 bytes each, of which $2900 reads only byte 0 (the position), 6 (the next template) and 8 (the rate): a stripe speeds up as it comes down the ground. The other bytes repeat the ground objects' pictures with expand flags.
The crash sound, 25 bytes loaded into the sound chip by $2400, which then gates the three voices: noise at three low pitches ($01C2, $0200, $0100), each with a long decay.
"  STRAFFING RUN AIRCRAFT NO.  ", shown by $2B00 with the plane's number after it; the game spells it with two Fs.
"     PRESS FIRE TO CONTINUE      ", the prompt of $2B00 and $2E30.
"       DISTANCE TO TARGET       ", put back under the bar after the result ($2E30).
Where each level's target pictures come from, two bytes a level: $3000, $3800, $9800, $9000 for levels 0-3, and $7800 in the four slots no level reaches.
High byte of the first level's target source.
Pointers to the four result messages by rating, lowest first: $8C00, $8BE0, $8BC0, $8BA0, and $8C00 in four slots no rating reaches.
High byte of the first result pointer.
"   WELL DONE-TARGET DESTROYED   ", for 64 hits or more.
" TARGET SUSTAINED HEAVY DAMAGE  ", for 48 hits or more.
"    TARGET PARTIALLY DAMAGED    ", for 16 hits or more.
"TARTARGET UNDAMAGED-TRY AGAIN", for fewer than 16 hits: the game shows "TARTARGET", a slip in the text. The zero bytes after it up to $8CFF are not read.

The hill panorama's top row, 40 screen codes read by column ($2F80, $2FB0) and copied to screen row 5 at the start ($24F0). The rest of the page repeats the next two rows as laid out on screen and is not read.
The hill panorama's middle row, 40 screen codes; the rest of the page is not read.

Entry table of Rob Hubbard's music driver: $A000 starts the tune ($ADD0), $A003 stops it ($AE09), $A006 plays one tick. The game calls only $A000, before each title screen ($14F0).

One tick of the music, for the three voices, the third first (register offsets 14, 7 and 0 from $A3ED). Counts the tick in $A426 and the speed counter $A418 (reloaded from $A419, so a step every second tick). On a new step, when a voice's note length $A3F7 runs out, reads the next byte of its pattern: the track at ($A527/$A52A) names the pattern ($FF restarts the track), the pattern pointers at $A52D/$A555 locate it. A note byte gives the length (bits 0-4), tie (bit 6) and whether an instrument or portamento byte follows (bit 7), then the note number, whose frequency comes from the table at $A32D; the instrument's eight bytes at $A427 + 8n set waveform, pulse width and envelope. Between steps it releases the gate at the note's end and runs the instrument's effects: vibrato scaled from the gap to the next semitone, pulse-width sweep, portamento, drum and pitch-drop effects, and an octave arpeggio on alternate ticks.
The music's frequency table: 96 notes of two bytes, low byte first, from $0116 up.
High bytes of the frequency table, read with $A32D as pairs.
The next note's frequency, which the vibrato reads to scale its depth to a semitone.
High byte of the next note's frequency.

Gate mask: $FF for a new note, $FE for a tied one.

Saved voice number, or the portamento step.

The speed: a step every $A419 + 1 ticks.
The instrument's offset into the table.
Each voice's frequency high byte, for portamento, the drum and the pitch drop ($A2E7).
Each voice's frequency low byte.
Each voice's portamento: step in bits 1-6, direction in bit 0.
The instrument's effect bits: 1 drum, 2 pitch drop, 4 octave arpeggio, 8 pulse sweep.
Pulse-width step.
The tick counter.

The instruments, eight bytes each: pulse width low and high, waveform, attack and decay, sustain and release, vibrato depth, pulse speed, effect bits; fifteen are set, the rest of the 32 slots to $A526 are zero.
Instrument byte 1, pulse width high.
Instrument byte 2, waveform.

Low bytes of the three tracks' addresses ($A57D, $A595, $A5AD); the high bytes follow at $A52A.
High bytes of the three tracks' addresses.

Low bytes of the 40 patterns' addresses; the high bytes follow at $A555, and after them the three tracks (pattern numbers, $FF to repeat) and the patterns themselves from $A60E to $ADCF, each ending with $FF.
High bytes of the 40 patterns' addresses.
The first voice's track: 23 pattern numbers, then $FF to repeat.
The second voice's track: 23 pattern numbers, then $FF.
The third voice's track, the bass and drums: 96 pattern numbers, then $FF.
The 40 patterns: note bytes as $A006 reads them, each pattern ending with $FF.
The music's patterns, continued to $ADCF.
Starts the title music: points the IRQ vector at $AE03, turns off the raster interrupt, sets CIA1 timer A to $4800 cycles and enables its interrupt, then resets the three voices' positions ($AE1E).
The music's interrupt: plays one tick ($A006) and goes on to the KERNAL's interrupt routine at $EA7E.

The driver's stop entry ($A003 jumps here), which the game never calls: puts the system interrupt back ($EA31), writes 0 to the volume and gates off the three voices through $AE31, which then sets the volume back to 15.
Clears each voice's track position, pattern position, note length and note, then (entry $AE31, also used by $AE09) gates off the three voices and sets the volume to 15.
Entry used by $AE09: gates off the three voices and sets the volume to 15.
